item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00124","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C08","C02","C07"],"selected_candidate_label":"C08","confidence":0.9,"relationship_type":"literal_language_template","rationale":"C08 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child's central appeal: both letters ask an audience to press Congress for funding action needed to continue an established program, followed by the distinctive construction “Only in this way can we continue...” C02 is also relevant because it closely parallels the pay-as-you-go taxation and adequate-revenue argument, while C07 shares the highway-program and congressional-funding context but less distinctive language.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I would hope that the Western Association of State Highway Officials would join me in urging the Congress to support an appropriate proposal to bring new revenues into the Highway Trust Fund. Only in this way can we continue the pay-as-you-go principle ... and keep the interstate program on schedule.","parent_excerpt":"I earnestly hope that the House will join with the Senate in approving this authorization, so this Government may continue to support the Children's fund. ... Only in this way can we honor the decision of the United Nations to keep this important program going until the end of 1953.","explanation":"Both passages combine an appeal for others to support congressional action, continuation of an existing program, and the distinctive transition “Only in this way can we...”"},{"child_excerpt":"the desirability of continuing the program on schedule and without interruption","parent_excerpt":"so this Government may continue to support the Children's fund ... keep this important program going","explanation":"The shared operative purpose is preserving uninterrupted continuation of an established program through congressional funding action."}]}
